label: HMRC update · 16 November 2026
title: Taking on Christmas staff? The new starter checklist HMRC expects you to follow
summary: HMRC says almost 80,000 people started a job last November. If you are hiring seasonal staff, here is what to collect from them, what to do without a P45 and when HMRC must hear about them.
body:
On 16 November 2026 HMRC published a press release encouraging people starting seasonal work to use the HMRC app. HMRC says almost 80,000 people started a job in November last year, in roles such as delivery driving, retail and hospitality. For small employers taking on extra staff for Christmas, the other side of this is getting each new starter set up correctly on payroll from day one.

Why it matters

HMRC's own survey, carried out between 27 February and 12 March 2026 among more than 5,200 people, found that 36% lack confidence with job-related paperwork and one in five jobseekers had delayed starting a job because of confusion about tax or paperwork. HMRC's November 2026 Agent Update also reminds employers to ask new employees for their full name, date of birth and National Insurance number before they start, and to use their P45 or the online starter checklist. Getting these details right first time is the simplest way to avoid emergency tax codes and payroll corrections later.

The steps before the first payday

GOV.UK sets out the steps in order. You must be registered as an employer first.

  • Check they need to be paid through PAYE.
  • Get employee information so you can work out their tax code and starter declaration.
  • Find out if they need to repay a student loan.
  • Set them up in your payroll software using these details.
  • Register them with HMRC on a Full Payment Submission (FPS). You must tell HMRC about a new employee on or before their first payday.

The usual employer duties still apply, including checking the person has the right to work in the UK.

What to collect

From the employee directly you need their date of birth, gender, full address and start date. From their P45 you get their full name, the date they left their last job, total pay and tax to date for the current tax year, whether student loan deductions should continue, their National Insurance number and their existing tax code. Keep this in your payroll records for the current year and the 3 following tax years.

  • No P45: ask them to complete HMRC's starter checklist. You also need one if they left their last job before 6 April 2025.
  • Two P45s: use the one with the latest leaving date and give the other back. If the dates are the same, use the one with the highest tax-free allowance.

If the P45 turns up late

Seasonal workers often hand in paperwork after their first payday. If HMRC has already sent you a tax code, use that code. If not, use the late P45 to work out the tax code and, where they left their last job after 5 April 2025, update total pay and tax to date in your software. A late starter checklist updates the starter declaration, and you keep using the tax code from your first FPS until HMRC sends a new one. Do not enter another start date on the next FPS.

Student loans

Ask every new starter whether they have a student loan or postgraduate loan, even if they have a P45. If they cannot tell you which plan they are on, use Plan 5 until you receive an SL1 start notice from HMRC. A postgraduate loan can be deducted at the same time as a student loan, but only one student loan plan at a time. Only stop deductions when HMRC sends form SL2 or PGL2, not because the employee asks.

Point your staff to the HMRC app

HMRC says the app lets workers find their National Insurance number, tax code, employment history and PAYE details. Pointing new starters to it can save time when you need their details quickly.

If you are taking on seasonal staff and want payroll set up and reported correctly, we can run it for you or check your new starter process before the first payday.
